Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,

automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# richgo

Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)

## Description

richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.

## Installation

### Using go get

```
go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
```

### Using homebrew

```
brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo
```

### Using asdf

```
asdf plugin add richgo
asdf install richgo 0.3.6
```

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```sh
richgo test ./...
```

### In an existing pipeline

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

### Creating an alias

You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:

* bash: `~/.bashrc`
* zsh: `~/.zshrc`

```
alias go=richgo
```

## Configuration

### Configuration file paths

It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:

* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`

Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.

### Configuration file format

Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.

```yaml
# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
labelType: (long | short | none)

# Style of "Build" lines.
buildStyle:
  # Hide lines
  hide: (true | false)
  # Bold or increased intensity.
  bold: (true | false)
  faint: (true | false)
  italic: (true | false)
  underline: (true | false)
  blinkSlow: (true | false)
  blinkRapid: (true | false)
  # Swap the foreground color and background color.
  inverse: (true | false)
  conceal: (true | false)
  crossOut: (true | false)
  frame: (true | false)
  encircle: (true | false)
  overline: (true | false)
  # Fore-color of text
  foreground: ("#xxxxxx" | rgb(0-256,0-256,0-256) | rgb(0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF) | (name of colors))
  # Back-color of text
  background: # Same format as `foreground`

# Style of the "Start" lines.
startStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" lines.
passStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" lines.
failStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Skip" lines.
skipStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "File" lines.
fileStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Line" lines.
lineStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
passPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" package lines.
failPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# A threshold of the coverage
coverThreshold: (0-100)

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is higher than coverThreshold.
coveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is lower than coverThreshold.
uncoveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# If you want to delete lines, write the regular expressions.
removals:
  - (regexp)
# If you want to leave `Test` prefixes, set it "true".
leaveTestPrefix: (true | false)
```

### Line categories

Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:

* **Build**: Build error messages
* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines

Each category can be styled separately.

### Label types

* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

buildStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
startStyle:

The bright-black is used for background color in Solarized dark theme. Richgo uses that color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle", so "START" and "SKIP" lines may not be visible on screens with Solarized dark theme.

startStyle:

By default, `richgo` determines whether or not to colorize its output based on whether it's connected to a TTY or not. This works for most use cases, but may not behave as expected if you use `richgo` in a pipeline of commands.

RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1 richgo test ./... | tee test.log

# richgo

Rich-Go will enrich `go test` outputs with text decorations.

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/99810.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/99810)

## Description

richgo is a command-line tool that adds color and formatting to the output of Go's `go test` command, making test results easier to read and understand.

## Installation

### Using go get

```
go get -u github.com/kyoh86/richgo
```

### Using homebrew

```
brew install kyoh86/tap/richgo
```

### Using asdf

```
asdf plugin add richgo
asdf install richgo 0.3.6
```

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```sh
richgo test ./...
```

### In an existing pipeline

If your build scripts expect to interact with the standard output format of `go test` (for instance, if you're using [go-junit-report](https://github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report)), you'll need to use the `testfilter` subcommand of `richgo`.

For example:

```sh
go test ./... | tee >(richgo testfilter) | go-junit-report
```

This will "tee" the output of the standard `go test` run into a `richgo testfilter` process as well as passing the original output to `go-junit-report`.

### Creating an alias

You can define an alias so that `go test` prints rich outputs:

* bash: `~/.bashrc`
* zsh: `~/.zshrc`

```
alias go=richgo
```

## Configuration

### Configuration file paths

It's possible to change styles with a preference file. Rich-Go loads preferences from the files in the following order:

* `${CWD}/.richstyle`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${CWD}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOPATH}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${GOROOT}/.richstyle.yml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yaml`
* `${HOME}/.richstyle.yml`

Setting the environment variable `RICHGO_LOCAL` to 1, Rich-Go loads only `${CWD}/.richstyle*`.

### Configuration file format

Rich-Go supports YAML formatted configuration files.

```yaml
# Type of the label that notes a kind of each lines.
labelType: (long | short | none)

# Style of "Build" lines.
buildStyle:
  # Hide lines
  hide: (true | false)
  # Bold or increased intensity.
  bold: (true | false)
  faint: (true | false)
  italic: (true | false)
  underline: (true | false)
  blinkSlow: (true | false)
  blinkRapid: (true | false)
  # Swap the foreground color and background color.
  inverse: (true | false)
  conceal: (true | false)
  crossOut: (true | false)
  frame: (true | false)
  encircle: (true | false)
  overline: (true | false)
  # Fore-color of text
  foreground: ("#xxxxxx" | rgb(0-256,0-256,0-256) | rgb(0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF,0x00-0xFF) | (name of colors))
  # Back-color of text
  background: # Same format as `foreground`

# Style of the "Start" lines.
startStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" lines.
passStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" lines.
failStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Skip" lines.
skipStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "File" lines.
fileStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Line" lines.
lineStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Pass" package lines.
passPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Fail" package lines.
failPackageStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# A threshold of the coverage
coverThreshold: (0-100)

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is higher than coverThreshold.
coveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# Style of the "Cover" lines with the coverage that is lower than coverThreshold.
uncoveredStyle:
  # Same format as `buildStyle`

# If you want to delete lines, write the regular expressions.
removals:
  - (regexp)
# If you want to leave `Test` prefixes, set it "true".
leaveTestPrefix: (true | false)
```

### Line categories

Rich-Go separates the output lines into the following categories:

* **Build**: Build error messages
* **Start**: Test start lines (e.g., `=== RUN   TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Pass**: Test pass lines (e.g., `--- PASS: TestSampleOK/SubtestOK`)
* **Fail**: Test failure lines (e.g., `--- FAIL: TestSampleNG (0.00s)`)
* **Skip**: Test skip lines (e.g., `--- SKIP: TestSampleSkip (0.00s)`)
* **PassPackage**: Package pass indicator (`PASS`)
* **FailPackage**: Package fail indicator (`FAIL`)
* **Cover**: Coverage analysis lines

Each category can be styled separately.

### Label types

* **Long**: BUILD, START, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, COVER
* **Short**: !!, >, o, x, -, %
* **None**: Rich-Go will never output labels.

### Default configuration

```yaml
labelType: long
buildStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
startStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passStyle:
  foreground: green
failStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
skipStyle:
  foreground: lightBlack
passPackageStyle:
  foreground: green
  hide: true
failPackageStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: red
  hide: true
coverThreshold: 50
coveredStyle:
  foreground: green
uncoveredStyle:
  bold: true
  foreground: yellow
fileStyle:
  foreground: cyan
lineStyle:
  foreground: magenta
```

### Solarized Dark theme compatibility

The bright-black is used for background color in Solarized dark theme. Richgo uses that color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle", so "START" and "SKIP" lines may not be visible on screens with Solarized dark theme.

To resolve that conflict, you can set another color for "startStyle" and "skipStyle" in your `.richstyle` file:

```yaml

  foreground: yellow

skipStyle:
  foreground: lightYellow
```

## Overriding colorization detection

By default, `richgo` determines whether or not to colorize its output based on whether it's connected to a TTY or not. This works for most use cases, but may not behave as expected if you use `richgo` in a pipeline of commands.

To force colorization, add `RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR=1` to the environment:

```sh

```

## Getting the version

If you want to get the version of `richgo`, this information is embedded in the binary (since Go 1.18). You can view it with `go version -m`:

```console
$ go version -m $(command -v richgo)
./richgo: go1.18
	path	github.com/kyoh86/richgo
	mod	github.com/kyoh86/richgo	v0.3.10	h1:iSGvcjhtQN2IVrBDhPk0if0R/RMQnCN1E/9OyAW4UUs=
	[...]
```

With POSIX `awk`:

```console
$ go version -m $(command -v richgo) | awk '$1 == "mod" && $2 == "github.com/kyoh86/richgo" {print $3;}'

```

try:
    out,err=p.communicate(timeout=2)

except Exception as e:

os.close(m_in)

package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
)

// lineProcessor turns input lines into output bytes.
type lineProcessor interface {
	processLine(line string) []byte
}

// richProcessor adapts a lineParser to the lineProcessor interface.
type richProcessor struct{ parser *lineParser }

func (r *richProcessor) processLine(line string) []byte { return r.parser.processLine(line) }

// plainProcessor passes lines through unchanged.
type plainProcessor struct{}

func (plainProcessor) processLine(line string) []byte { return []byte(line + "\n") }

// lineWriter is an io.Writer that splits a byte stream into lines and
// writes the processed lines to an underlying writer.
type lineWriter struct {
	out  *os.File
	proc lineProcessor
	buf  []byte
}

func newLineWriter(out *os.File, proc lineProcessor) *lineWriter {
	return &lineWriter{out: out, proc: proc}
}

func dropCR(line string) string {
	return strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\r")
}

func (w *lineWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	w.buf = append(w.buf, p...)
	for {
		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.buf, '\n')
		if idx < 0 {
			break
		}
		raw := string(w.buf[:idx])
		w.buf = w.buf[idx+1:]
		if out := w.proc.processLine(dropCR(raw)); out != nil {
			_, _ = w.out.Write(out)
		}
	}
	return len(p), nil
}

// flushRich processes a final unterminated line, if any.
func (w *lineWriter) flushRich() {
	if len(w.buf) == 0 {
		return
	}
	raw := string(w.buf)
	w.buf = nil
	if out := w.proc.processLine(dropCR(raw)); out != nil {
		_, _ = w.out.Write(out)
	}
}

// flushPlain writes a final unterminated line, or a single newline when
// the stream ended with a newline (or had no output at all).
func (w *lineWriter) flushPlain() {
	if len(w.buf) == 0 {
		_, _ = w.out.Write([]byte("\n"))
		return
	}
	raw := string(w.buf)
	w.buf = nil
	if out := w.proc.processLine(dropCR(raw)); out != nil {
		_, _ = w.out.Write(out)
	}
}

func isTerminal(fd uintptr) bool {
	// ioctl TCGETS on Linux.
	var termios [64]byte
	_, _, errno := syscall.Syscall(syscall.SYS_IOCTL, fd, uintptr(0x5401), uintptr(unsafePointer(&termios[0])))
	return errno == 0
}

func colorable() bool {
	if os.Getenv("RICHGO_FORCE_COLOR") != "" {
		return true
	}
	return isTerminal(os.Stderr.Fd())
}

// exitForExitError terminates the process with the command's exit code
// when err reports that the command ran and exited (or was signalled).
func exitForExitError(err error) {
	if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
		os.Exit(exitErr.ExitCode())
	}
}

func main() {
	cfg := loadConfig()
	args := os.Args[1:]

	if len(args) > 0 && (args[0] == "test" || args[0] == "testfilter") {
		var cmd *exec.Cmd
		if args[0] == "test" {
			cmd = exec.Command("go", args...)
		} else {
			cmd = exec.Command("cat", "-")
		}
		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin

		if colorable() {
			outWriter := newLineWriter(os.Stdout, &richProcessor{parser: newLineParser(&cfg)})
			errWriter := newLineWriter(os.Stderr, &richProcessor{parser: newLineParser(&cfg)})
			cmd.Stdout = outWriter
			cmd.Stderr = errWriter
			err := cmd.Run()
			if err != nil {
				exitForExitError(err)
				outWriter.flushRich()
				errWriter.flushRich()
				panic(err)
			}
			outWriter.flushRich()
			errWriter.flushRich()
			return
		}

		outWriter := newLineWriter(os.Stdout, plainProcessor{})
		errWriter := newLineWriter(os.Stderr, plainProcessor{})
		cmd.Stdout = outWriter
		cmd.Stderr = errWriter
		err := cmd.Run()
		if err != nil {
			exitForExitError(err)
			outWriter.flushPlain()
			errWriter.flushPlain()
			panic(err)
		}
		outWriter.flushPlain()
		errWriter.flushPlain()
		return
	}

	// Every other command is forwarded to the real go tool.
	cmd := exec.Command("go", args...)
	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	err := cmd.Run()
	if err != nil {
		exitForExitError(err)
		panic(err)
	}
}

func stdColor(code int) colorValue { return colorValue{kind: colorStandard, code: code} }

func defaultConfig() Config {
	return Config{
		LabelType: "long",
		BuildStyle: Style{
			Bold:       true,
			Foreground: stdColor(33),
		},
		StartStyle: Style{Foreground: stdColor(90)},

		FailStyle: Style{

		},
		SkipStyle:        Style{Foreground: stdColor(90)},
		PassPackageStyle: Style{Hide: true, Foreground: stdColor(32)},
		FailPackageStyle: Style{Hide: true, Bold: true, Foreground: stdColor(31)},
		CoverThreshold:   50,
		CoveredStyle:     Style{Foreground: stdColor(32)},
		UncoveredStyle:   Style{Bold: true, Foreground: stdColor(33)},
		FileStyle:        Style{Foreground: stdColor(36)},
		LineStyle:        Style{Foreground: stdColor(35)},
	}
}

func (c Config) clone() Config {
	out := c
	if c.Removals != nil {
		out.Removals = append([]string(nil), c.Removals...)
	}
	return out
}

func effectiveGopath() string {
	gopath := os.Getenv("GOPATH")
	if gopath == "" {
		if home := os.Getenv("HOME"); home != "" {
			gopath = filepath.Join(home, "go")
		} else {
			gopath = ""
		}
	}
	return gopath
}

func configCandidatePaths() []string {
	var paths []string
	add := func(base string) {
		for _, name := range []string{".richstyle", ".richstyle.yaml", ".richstyle.yml"} {
			paths = append(paths, filepath.Join(base, name))
		}
	}
	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		cwd = ""
	}
	add(cwd)
	if os.Getenv("RICHGO_LOCAL") != "1" {
		add(effectiveGopath())
		add(runtime.GOROOT())
		if home := os.Getenv("HOME"); home != "" {
			add(home)
		}
	}
	return paths
}

func loadConfig() Config {
	cfg := defaultConfig()
	for _, path := range configCandidatePaths() {
		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
				continue
			}
			log.Printf("error reading from %s :  %s", path, err)
			continue
		}
		next := cfg.clone()
		if err := applyYAMLConfig(&next, string(data)); err != nil {
			log.Printf("error unmarshaling yaml from %s :  %s", path, err)
			continue
		}
		cfg = next
	}
	return cfg
}

type lineKind int

const (
	kindGeneric lineKind = iota
	kindBuild
	kindStart
	kindPass

	kindBareFail
)

type parsedLine struct {

	style       *Style
	label       string // logical label text (PASS, BUILD, ...) or "" for generic/bare
	content     string
	updateState bool
	bare        bool
	special     bool // formatted output has no trailing newline added by the writer (the newline is part of the styled text)
}

var (
	fileLineRe     = regexp.MustCompile(`([^\s:]+\.go)(:\d+(?::\d+)?)`)
	buildBracketRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^# (\S+) (\[[^\s\[\]]+\])$`)
	buildSingleRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^# ([^ ]*)$`)
	testResultRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^[ \t]*--- (PASS|FAIL|SKIP): Test`)
	bareRe         = regexp.MustCompile(`^(PASS|FAIL)[ \t]*$`)
	failPackageRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^FAIL([ \t]+\S+[ \t]+(?:[\d.]+\w+|\[build failed\]))$`)
	skipPackageRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^\?[ \t]+(\S+[ \t]+\[(?:no test files|no tests to run)\])$`)
	coverRe        = regexp.MustCompile(`^coverage: (\d+\.\d)% of statements$`)
	okCoverageRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]+([\d.]+\w+|\(cached\))[ \t]+(coverage:[ \t]+\d+\.\d+% of statements)[ \t]*$`)
	okNoTestsRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]+([\d.]+\w+|\(cached\))[ \t]+\[no tests to run\]$`)
	okSimpleRe     = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]+([\d.]+\w+|\(cached\))[ \t]*$`)
	okBracketRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]+\[no tests to run\]$`)
	okTrailingRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]+$`)
	okBareRe       = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+(\S+)$`)
	okEmptyRe      = regexp.MustCompile(`^ok[ \t]+$`)
)

type lineParser struct {
	cfg       *Config
	removals  []*regexp.Regexp
	state     *Style
	zeroState Style
}

func newLineParser(cfg *Config) *lineParser {
	p := &lineParser{cfg: cfg}
	p.state = &p.zeroState
	for _, pattern := range cfg.Removals {
		p.removals = append(p.removals, regexp.MustCompile(pattern))
	}
